question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{′}-y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}∼{{field-1}} & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-3}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\  & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))+{b}_{n}\cdot \frac{n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{′}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\  & \,-(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\  & \,\,=-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned} & -\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}-{a}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & \,\,+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}-{b}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & \,\,\,\,=-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, equating the free terms and the coefficients next to sines and cosines, we obtain the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=-1 \\ \frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}-{a}_{n}=\frac{4}{{n}^{2}\pi } \\ -\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}-{b}_{n}=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, ${a}_{0}=2,$ which means the constant term is given by

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=1.
$$

Next, from the third equation, ${b}_{n}=-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}.$ Substituting this into the third equation, gives

$$
(-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2})\frac{n\pi }{2}-{a}_{n}=\frac{4}{{n}^{2}\pi }\,⇒\,{a}_{n}=-\frac{16}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+4)}.
$$

Therefore, for ${a}_{n}$ with $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2} \\  & =-\frac{n\pi }{2}\cdot (-\frac{16}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+4)}) \\  & =\frac{8}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}∼1 & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{16}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+4)}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{8}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+4)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
